newsitem.title: USA: Varlen sees record FY 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Varlen sees record FY 1997 earnings.

text.p: Varlen Corp expects to report record sales and earnings for fiscal 1997, president and chief executive Richard Wellek said Tuesday.

According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates is $2.40 a share for fiscal 1997, an 18 percent increase over the previous year's $2.04, excluding a $0.23 gain from the sale of a business. Varlen reported fiscal 1996 sales of $409.5 million.
"I think the analysts have done a very good job of understanding our business," Wellek said of the consensus estimate. "We have momentum. We expect to have record sales and earnings this year."
Varlen's fiscal year ends on January 31.
Wellek told Reuters that he expected the company would likely maintain or exceed its 16 percent increase in its first quarter truck/trailer segment sales.

"Because the freight liner Century class truck is increasing in production, the market is stronger," Wellek said. "So it isn't hard to conclude that the opportunity to grow at 16 percent, or greater, for the year, is there."

Wellek told investors that the company expected $7 to $8 million in sales of its MD automatic transmission component to Ford Motor Co this year. He said production for Ford's 1998 model year will begin in July.
"This year's revenue will be an additional seven to eight million, and we'll lose money in that business in the first half during the start-up period," Wellek said.
"But as we move to full production, on an annualized basis, that will represent $16 to 17 million in incremental revenues dependent on Ford's production rates," he said.
Varlen manufactures railroad, truck/trailer and automotive components and petroleum analyzers.
